title: Telesat prepared to execute FCC Upper C-band transition plan | Telesat
summary: Telesat is preparing to execute its FCC Upper C-band transition plan, with eligibility for US$189 million in incentive payments and approved cost reimbursement.
body_text: OTTAWA, CANADA – July 27, 2026 – Telesat GEO Inc, a subsidiary of Telesat Corporation (NASDAQ and TSX: TSAT) (“Telesat”), one of the world’s largest and most innovative satellite operators, is preparing to execute its Upper C-band transition plan following the U.S. Federal Communications Commission’s (FCC’s) adoption of its Upper C-band Report and Order (“Order”). The Order establishes the framework for repurposing 160 MHz of Upper C-band spectrum in the contiguous United States for next-generation terrestrial wireless services. As set forth in the FCC’s Order, Telesat GEO Inc. is eligible to receive US$189 million in incentive payments, contingent upon meeting the specified transition deadlines. The order also confirms reimbursement of reasonable and necessary transition costs as approved by the clearinghouse. “The FCC’s Order establishes a clear path forward for the Upper C-band transition and will help accelerate the availability of spectrum needed to expand next-generation wireless services,” stated Dan Goldberg, Telesat’s President and CEO. “Building on our successful execution of the previous C-band transition, we look forward to working closely with customers, earth station operators, and regulators to efficiently clear this spectrum while ensuring continuity of services.” The FCC’s Order requires satellite operators to submit transition plans by November 5, 2026, outlining the steps necessary to clear the designated spectrum. Telesat GEO Inc. will continue to engage with affected stakeholders to support a smooth transition and maintain reliable satellite services throughout the process. Media Contact: pr@telesat.com

title: Unveiling the Hidden Dangers: Exploring the Side Effects of Lunesta
body_text: Explore the potential side effects of Lunesta and learn how to reduce discomfort while ensuring a peaceful night's rest. Take the first step towards improving your sleep with Sleep Reset. Start by taking our sleep quiz , enabling us to pinpoint your key issues. Following the quiz, opt to work with your personal sleep coach and gain access to our dedicated sleep program. It's a proactive approach to address sleep concerns without the risks associated with medications like Lunesta. Sleeping Pills vs. Sleep Reset Understanding Lunesta: What Is It? If you've been lying awake at 3 AM wondering if that prescription bottle on your nightstand might finally give you some peace, you're not alone. Lunesta (the fancy name is eszopiclone) is basically your brain's chill pill when it comes to sleep. Here's the simple version: Your brain has a natural chemical called GABA that's like your body's built-in "time for bed" signal. Sometimes that signal gets weak or gets drowned out by stress, anxiety, or just life being life. Lunesta comes in and turns up the volume on that signal, helping your brain actually listen when it's time to wind down. Think of it like this – if your brain is a noisy house party that won't quiet down, Lunesta is like having someone turn down the music and dim the lights so everyone knows it's time to chill.If you've been lying awake at 3 AM wondering if that prescription bottle on your nightstand might finally give you some peace, you're not alone. Lunesta (eszopiclone) is a non-benzodiazepine hypnotic medication, part of what doctors call "Z-drugs," specifically designed to treat insomnia. The Clinical Mechanism: Lunesta works as a positive allosteric modulator of the GABA-A receptor complex. In simpler terms, your brain has a natural chemical called gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) that's like your body's built-in "time for bed" signal. Sometimes that signal gets weak or gets drowned out by stress, anxiety, or just life being life. Lunesta comes in and turns up the volume on that signal by enhancing GABA's inhibitory effects on neural activity. Pharmacokinetics (The Technical Stuff): Onset: Takes effect within 30 minutes to 1 hour Half-life: Approximately 6 hours (longer than immediate-release zolpidem) Peak plasma concentration: Reached within 1-2 hours Metabolism: Primarily through the liver via CYP3A4 and CYP2E1 enzymes Elimination: About 75% excreted in urine Think of it like this – if your brain is a noisy house party that won't quiet down, Lunesta is like having someone turn down the music and dim the lights so everyone knows it's time to chill. Who Should Take Lunesta? Let's be honest here – Lunesta isn't for everyone, and it's definitely not a magic fix for the occasional restless night. Clinical Indications: Doctors typically prescribe eszopiclone for: Primary insomnia (difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or early morning awakening) Sleep maintenance insomnia specifically Chronic insomnia lasting more than 4 weeks When sleep disturbances significantly impair daytime functioning Standard Dosing: Adults: 1-3 mg taken immediately before bedtime Elderly patients (65+): Starting dose of 1 mg (due to slower metabolism) Hepatic impairment: Maximum 2 mg Duration: FDA-approved for up to 6 months of continuous use Contraindications (When You Absolutely Shouldn't Take It): Known hypersensitivity to eszopiclone Severe hepatic impairment Myasthenia gravis Severe respiratory depression Sleep apnea syndrome Acute narrow-angle glaucoma Important Drug Interactions: CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin): Can increase Lunesta levels significantly CNS depressants (opioids, benzodiazepines, alcohol): Additive sedative effects Rifampin: Reduces Lunesta effectiveness by up to 80% Olanzapine: Increased risk of complex sleep behaviors Is Lunesta Right for You? As Dr. Daniel Jin Blum, Sleep Expert, Clinical Psychologist, Research Assistant Professor of Psychology puts it: “Over time, users may need higher doses or experience rebound insomnia when stopping, this is why behavioral options are often preferred.” What he means is that Lunesta is not a forever solution. Lunesta may be a good option for individuals struggling with chronic insomnia who have not found relief through lifestyle changes alone. However, it should be used under the guidance of a healthcare provider and only for short-term treatment due to the risk of dependence. Common Side Effects of Lunesta Look, every medication comes with baggage, and Lunesta is no exception. Here's the clinical breakdown of what you might deal with: We asked Dr. Shiyan Yeo, Internal Medicine Physician, Sleep Medicine Expert about what side effects one might experience. She says: “Lunesta can cause memory issues, dizziness, and next-day impairment, especially in older adults.” Ultimately, Lunesta, despite its sleep-enhancing capabilities, comes with a set of common side effects . When it comes to Lunesta, it might be helpful for people with stubborn insomnia who haven’t found relief through lifestyle changes. Still, it’s important to use it only for a short period, under a healthcare provider’s supervision, due to the risk of dependence. So, basically, pills can help, but they’re not a magic fix—and they shouldn’t be your first choice. Drowsiness Lunesta doesn’t just make you sleepy, it can leave you feeling very drowsy. We’re not talking a little yawn here and there; this is the kind of drowsiness that hangs around like an unwanted houseguest. Drowsiness can persist into the day after taking Lunesta May interfere with driving or operating machinery Can disrupt cognitive functions and reaction times Possible impact on work productivity and social interactions Some individuals may experience a slowed breathing rate during sleep Headache Headaches are one of those annoying little surprises some people get when they start taking Lunesta. You might brush it off as just another headache, but if it pops up right after you start a new medicine like Lunesta, it makes you stop and scratch your head. Is it the pill? Either way, it’s worth paying attention to, no one wants an extra migraine as a side dish with their sleep aid. The active ingredient in Lunesta, eszopiclone, can cause temporary changes in brain chemistry which may lead to headaches. In response to the foreign substance, the body might attempt to flush out Lunesta, manifesting in headaches. Those with a sensitivity or allergy to Lunesta may experience headaches as a response. Increased pressure in the brain due to the sedative effects of Lunesta can cause headaches. Dry Mouth Lunesta can also make your mouth feeling like the Sahara. Dry mouth’s pretty common with this medicine and you might even get a bit dehydrated. Stay well-hydrated by drinking plenty of water Avoid alcohol and caffeine as they can further contribute to dryness Keep a glass of water by your bed when sleep Try a saliva substitute or a mouth moisturizing gel Chewing sugar-free gum or sucking on sugar-free hard candies can stimulate saliva production Maintain good oral hygiene to prevent dental problems associated with dry mouth Unpleasant Taste You ever popped a Lunesta and then, suddenly—your mouth tastes like you’ve been consuming a handful of rusty pennies? Lunesta can also leave your mouth with an unpleasant taste. Opt for a mouthwash or a palate-cleansing drink after taking Lunesta to combat the unpleasant taste. Pair it with a snack or meal, which can mask the flavor and make it easier to tolerate. Keep a candy or mint handy as it can assist in immediately addressing the unsettling taste. The unpleasant taste is generally temporary and tends to fade away once the medicine is fully metabolized. Nausea While not as prevalent as other side effects, nausea can occur in some individuals taking Lunesta. This unpleasant sensation can be unsettling and significantly decrease your quality of life. Stay hydrated and maintain regular meals Avoid foods that tend to exacerbate nausea Rest and avoid vigorous activities Consult your doctor if nausea becomes severe or persistent Serious Side Effects to Be Aware Of Encountering the more daunting realm of Lunesta's effects can be intimidating. Medical experts highlight memory problems, hallucinations, sleepwalking episodes, severe allergic reactions, and drastic changes in behavior as symptoms needing immediate attention. Some situations require immediate medical attention: Difficulty breathing or swallowing Swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat Severe confusion or memory loss Any "sleep activities" you don't remember Thoughts of hurting yourself Don't mess around with these – get help right away. It's critical to stay attentive to potentially grave symptoms including sleepwalking, sudden mental/mood changes, and uncharacteristic recklessness. If these or worsening symptoms emerge, prompt communication with your health provider is strongly advised. Memory Problems Lunesta has been known to affect memory, sometimes resulting in transient amnesia. This usually occurs when users fail to get a full night's sleep after taking the medication. Morning recall of nighttime events may be obscure or even completely lost. The paradox of losing memories after taking a sleep aid is indeed ironic. Despite aiding the brain to achieve rest, Lunesta can lead to unforeseen memory issues. The intrigue lies in the discrepancy between the desired restful sleep and the potential cognitive impact. Part of the 'hidden dangers' of Lunesta is the fear of memory loss. Users may experience difficulty remembering tasks or details, affecting their everyday life. The concerns underscore the importance of understanding possible side-effects before using any medication, and taking steps to mitigate them. Hallucinations One disquieting risk associated with Lunesta is the potential for hallucinations. Hallucinations, while uncommon, can materially disrupt daily life and become a distressing ordeal for the user. The effect of hallucinations, especially for individuals unacquainted with this phenomena, can be profoundly disturbing. The eerie experience of seeing, hearing, or feeling something that isn't there adds an unsettling layer to Lunesta's known side effects. Unraveling the impact of hallucinations as a side effect of Lunesta, it becomes vitally important to discuss this with healthcare professionals. This unnerving experience can cause undue stress and affects not just sleep, but the overall well-being of the person. Sleepwalking Taking Lunesta isn't just about getting to sleep, it can also result in unintended nighttime activities, including sleepwalking. This adverse event, while not usual, can put users at risk of accidental injuries. It's crucial to seek immediate help if this side effect begins. We often associate sleepwalking with children but under the influence of Lunesta, adults too may find themselves unexpectedly wandering at night. The underlying mechanism is unknown, but the hypnotic effect of the drug might play a role in inducing such activities. Although often brushed off as an oddity, Lunesta-induced sleepwalking poses serious concerns. The affected person could make complex maneuvers without any memory later, which can be dangerous. Should you experience this phenomena, it's imperative to inform your physician promptly. Allergic Reactions An allergic reaction to Lunesta could manifest as a rash, itching, or severe dizziness, and it's crucial to recognize these as potential red flags, rather than harmless bodily responses to the medication. Swelling of the face, throat, and tongue, along with difficulty breathing, warrants immediate medical attention. In the event of an unidentified allergic reaction to Lunesta, rapid heart rate, shakiness, anxiety, or confusion may be experienced as unseen side effects. Knowledge of these signs often aids individuals in seeking immediate and effective health intervention. Changes in Behavior Ingesting Lunesta might provoke unexpected changes in behavior. These can present as increased aggression, agitation, or confusion. It's crucial these events are reported to the doctor immediately to prevent any untoward incidents. Lunesta, while effective for sleep disorders, can induce atypical behavior in some. Users have reported activities such as sleep-driving and preparing food while asleep. This highlights the need to monitor the personality shifts that might emerge during medication. Enhanced prevalence of such unusual behaviors can be associated with Lunesta consumption. Being vigilant for these symptoms will ensure the safest, most effective use of this medication. One must always remember, health is holistic and doesn't merely represent an aspect of it. When to Seek Medical Help Some situations require immediate medical attention: Difficulty breathing or swallowing Swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat Severe confusion or memory loss Any "sleep activities" you don't remember Thoughts of hurting yourself If you notice unusual symptoms or side effects getting worse during your course of Lunesta, don't hesitate to reach out to your healthcare provider. Remember, they're there to guide you and adjust your treatment plan, if necessary, for the best outcome. Emergency Situations In dire circumstances, the unwanted reactions caused by Lunesta can be severe enough to necessitate immediate medical attention. Instances such as breathing difficulties, a serious rash, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat denote emergency situations and should be treated with urgency. If you encounter emergency cases due to Lunesta, stay calm, and take swift action. Dial your local emergency number or seek immediate help from any healthcare facility. Ensure safety by not engaging in activities requiring alertness, such as driving, until properly assessed by a professional. Contacting Your Healthcare Provider Ensure your safety post Lunesta intake by being vigilant about changes to your health. Contact your healthcare provider if you notice new side effects, an increase in existing ones, or if your insomnia symptoms persist despite medication. One cannot be too cautious when one's health is on the line. When side effects occur, especially those that disrupt your daily life, your doctor should be the first to know. The adage 'better safe than sorry' holds true, especially with prescription medication. Your healthcare provider is vital in navigating these potential side effects. Do not neglect to notify them of changes in your physical or mental state after the medication intake. Only through open dialogue can you ensure that Lunesta offers the best remedy for your insomnia. Tips for Minimizing Side Effects Adhering to your prescribed dosage, evading alcohol and other depressants, maintaining a stable sleep routine, and proactively reporting any unusual symptoms to your doctor can substantially limit Lunesta's side effects. Being knowledgeable of these precautions allows you to prevent potential risks, optimizing the benefits of this sleep aid and ensuring a peaceful night's rest. Follow the Prescribed Dosage Heeding the dosage stipulations when taking Lunesta is vital. Following a physician's directives decreases the risk of experiencing pronounced side effects and guards against adverse reactions such as severe drowsiness or dependency. Initial dose: 1 mg for elderly, 2 mg for adults Titration: May increase to 3 mg if 2 mg ineffective after 7-10 days Timing: Take immediately before bedtime with ≥7-8 hours available for sleep Duration: Reassess every 2-4 weeks; taper if used >2 weeks Stick to the Script: I know it's tempting to think "if one pill helps, two will help more," but resist that urge. Your doctor prescribed a specific amount for a reason. Doses above 3 mg haven't shown additional efficacy and significantly increase side effect risk. Overdosing or misusing Lunesta exerts substantial effects on the user. Moments of memory loss, erratic behavior, or even perilous activities like sleepwalking can be precipitated by stuffing one's system with an unwarranted amount of this substance. Respecting dosage instructions is therefore necessary for both safety and efficacy. Avoid Alcohol and Other Depressants Taking Lunesta alongside alcohol or other depressants escalates the sedative effect, bears unforeseen risks and detrimental consequences. From decreased respiratory function to severe drowsiness or responsive issues, it's a risk you don't want to take. Abstaining from alcohol and depressants while using Lunesta holds significant potential benefits. Apart from promoting the drug's effectiveness, it serves to decrease the possibility of harmful side effects and keeps you in control of your body and reactions. It's paramount to inform your healthcare provider about any consumption of alcohol or other depressants as these lower Lunesta's efficacy and safety. Practicing abstinence while on Lunesta contributes to achieving restful sleep, sans enhanced risk. Maintain a Consistent Sleep Schedule Maintaining regular sleep patterns is a critical strategy in managing the side effects of Lunesta. A consistent sleep schedule aids in the natural absorption and efficient utilization of the drug, minimizing potential side effects. Once you achieve a balanced sleep rhythm, you may find Lunesta's unwanted effects dwindling. A consistent sleep pattern can ensure optimal effectiveness of the drug while maximizing sleep quality. Having stability in your sleep-wake cycle while taking Lunesta proves potent in reducing the risk of disruptive side effects. Essentially, harmonizing your sleep routine with your medication intake can create a more efficient sleep environment. Report Any Unusual Symptoms to Your Doctor Taking responsibility for your own health is vital when using Lunesta. Promptly reporting unusual symptoms is crucial. This can help your healthcare provider adjust your medication or offer alternatives to manage your sleep problems without compromising your well-being. Remember the old adage, a stitch in time saves nine? It rings true for Lunesta users. Keep track of unusual symptoms and report them promptly to your doctor. Early detection helps in addressing potential complications, ensuring your sleep aid remains a boon - not a bane. Lunesta vs. Ambien: A Head-to-Head Battle for Better Sleep For individuals struggling with insomnia, two of the most commonly prescribed sleeping pills are Lunesta (eszopiclone) and Ambien (zolpidem). Both are effective in their own right, but key differences in their formulation, duration of action, and potential side effects make one a potentially better choice over the other depending on the specific nature of a person's sleep problems. The central question for many is: which one is more effective? The answer, as with many medications, is nuanced and depends on whether the primary difficulty is falling asleep, staying asleep, or a combination of both. The Key Difference: Sleep Onset vs. Sleep Maintenance The primary distinction in the effectiveness of Lunesta and Ambien lies in their half-life, the time it takes for the body to eliminate half of the drug. This pharmacological property directly influences how long the medication's effects last. Ambien (and its generic, zolpidem) generally has a shorter half-life. The immediate-release (IR) formulation is designed for rapid onset of action, making it highly effective for individuals who have trouble initiating sleep. However, its shorter duration may not be sufficient to prevent awakenings throughout the night. To address this, a controlled-release version, Ambien CR , was developed. It has a dual-layer tablet that releases one dose quickly to help with sleep onset and a second dose more slowly to aid in sleep maintenance. Lunesta (and its generic, eszopiclone) has a longer half-life than immediate-release Ambien. This extended duration of action makes it particularly beneficial for people who struggle with waking up frequently during the night or too early in the morning. While effective at promoting sleep onset, its strength lies in helping individuals stay asleep for a longer period. Head-to-Head Evidence: What the Studies Show Direct comparative studies and meta-analyses offer a more evidence-based look at their relative effectiveness. A number of head-to-head clinical trials have demonstrated that both medications are superior to placebo in improving sleep latency (the time it takes to fall asleep), reducing wake time after sleep onset (WASO), and increasing total sleep time. However, a consistent finding is that Lunesta generally shows a slight edge in promoting sleep maintenance. Studies have shown that patients taking eszopiclone tend to experience fewer nighttime awakenings and have a longer total sleep time compared to those on immediate-release zolpidem. When comparing Lunesta to Ambien CR, the differences in sleep maintenance are less pronounced, though some evidence suggests Lunesta may still provide a longer duration of sleep for some individuals. Regarding sleep onset, some studies suggest that immediate-release Ambien may have a slightly faster onset of action for some patients. It is important to note that individual responses to these medications can vary significantly. ‍ Clinical Efficacy Data Sleep Onset (Sleep Latency Reduction): Ambien IR: 12-15 minute reduction vs. placebo Lunesta: 10-12 minute reduction vs. placebo Winner: Slight edge to Ambien IR for faster onset Sleep Maintenance (Wake After Sleep Onset): Lunesta: 25-30 minute reduction in WASO Ambien IR: 10-15 minute reduction in WASO Ambien CR: 20-25 minute reduction in WASO Winner: Lunesta shows superior sleep maintenance Total Sleep Time: Lunesta: 30-45 minute increase Ambien IR: 20-30 minute increase Ambien CR: 35-40 minute increase Winner: Lunesta, with Ambien CR close second Side Effect Profiles: A Balancing Act Both Lunesta and Ambien belong to a class of drugs known as non-benzodiazepine hypnotics, or "Z-drugs." They share a similar mechanism of action by enhancing the effects of the neurotransmitter GABA in the brain, which promotes relaxation and sleep. Consequently, they also share a similar side effect profile. Common side effects for both medications include: Drowsiness Dizziness Headache Next-day grogginess or "hangover" effect Unpleasant taste (more commonly reported with Lunesta) Serious side effects for both can include: Complex sleep behaviors (e.g., sleepwalking, sleep-driving, making and eating food while asleep) with no memory of the event. This risk is a boxed warning from the FDA for both medications. Worsening of depression or suicidal thoughts. Allergic reactions. User reviews and patient-reported outcomes often highlight the distinctive unpleasant or metallic taste associated with Lunesta as a significant drawback for some. On the other hand, reports of memory impairment and amnesic behaviors are frequently mentioned in discussions about Ambien. The Verdict: Which Pill is the Right Fit? Deciding between Lunesta and Ambien is a collaborative process between a patient and their healthcare provider. The "more effective" pill is the one that best addresses the individual's specific sleep issues with the most manageable side effect profile. Choose Ambien IR if: Primary complaint is sleep initiation, elderly patient (lower hangover effect), cost considerations Choose Ambien CR if: Mixed sleep initiation and maintenance issues, want zolpidem with longer action Choose Lunesta if: Primary complaint is sleep maintenance, frequent awakenings, early morning awakening, need longer treatment duration Ultimately, the choice may also be influenced by factors such as insurance coverage, cost, and an individual's unique response and tolerance to each medication. A thorough discussion with a doctor about your sleep patterns, medical history, and any other medications you are taking is crucial to determining the most appropriate and effective treatment for your insomnia. Start Sleeping Better With Sleep Reset Today! Dr. Suzanne Gorovoy, Sleep Expert, Clinical Psychologist, Behavioral Sleep Medicine Specialist says this about behavioral interventions versus prescription medications and their impact on sleep: “Behavioral interventions are safer and often more effective than long-term use of prescription sedatives.” What she means is medications like Lunesta can be helpful in the short term, but they're not really solving the root problem. It's like taking painkillers for a broken bone without setting the bone first. Behavioral interventions like CBT-I are actually the gold standard for insomnia treatment in the medical world. title: Using Partner Marketing to Generate Leads
summary: How can you use partner marketing to grow?
body_text: Getting your partner marketing program in place is such a fun and exhilarating project, especially when it starts to yield results! Like any type of marketing or sales initiative, the goal is to always grow, improve and move forward. In regards to partner marketing, how do you grow? How do you find more partners to help leverage sales and drive revenue higher? This article will highlight 3 little tricks to put in place that will help you do just that by generating more leads through partner marketing. 1. Analytics and Insights You need a way to track the activity and sales results of your partners, so you can easily figure out what’s working, what’s not, and how to improve. There are a few great ways to do this that are relatively simple, especially if you have a partner marketing platform in place. If your current partner marketing platform can track different incentives for your different channels, great, you’re already halfway there. With different partner tiers and programs, you can easily track which campaigns are working well and which need improvement. Try using different codes to track the conversion rate, and voila, you’ve created measurable metrics. Want to know what your partners are driving from their own channels? Make sure each uses your trackable link so you can see the click count for each link. Again, being able to manage these links within your platform is key to gaining efficiency, and essentially generating more leads through partner marketing. 2. Sales and Marketing Materials As partner marketing efforts get more sophisticated, you are going to need to think about what kinds of content your partners are producing: How are they sharing your product? How does this align with your company's goals? In the initial stages, you should at least have an asset folder where your partners have access to basic sales and marketing materials. After that, build out a community content calendar or challenges for your partners, and continuously add new messaging, images and videos to your asset library. Circling back to point one, having one platform that provides this for you is easiest and most efficient. Having a one-stop-shop where your partners can view content at will can help leverage your partner relationships and help you grow over the long-term. 3. Partner Distribution Channel If you have multiple partners working with you, you must have put in the leg work to build those relationships - don’t lose them. The key to partner marketing is long-term relationships: the more you grow together, the bigger the payoff will be. The easiest way to stay connected is to send a monthly email to all of your past and current with upcoming opportunities for collaboration. Highlight great projects, discuss upcoming opportunities and foster your relationships with these partners. You can also create different drip marketing campaigns for your partners that send at different times depending on where they are in their relationship with your company. The key here is that you want to be able to automate this process. You have the ability to manage all 3 of these steps by incorporating one platform that manages your entire partner marketing program. In any type of initiative, efficiency is key. With all of these steps in place, you shouldn't have to manually do too much. You want to focus on scaling and growing and let your automated program do the heavy lifting for you. In the end, partner marketing is really all about relationships. It's about nurturing, managing and leveraging your relationships with your partners to scale your program - and sales and revenue - to the next level. If you can focus on the relationships, and not get bogged down by the mundane day-to-day, you’ll be able to bring your partner marketing to the next level in no time.

title: Stardust Increases Revenue by 4x in Just Six Weeks
summary: See how a popular health app got started with experimentation
body_text: Where this story begins Stardust is an app that stands out in the market. It was founded by a group of women who weren't happy with the cycle and pregnancy tracking apps they saw in the App Store. From their view, most apps in this space were too pink, too flowery, and were missing something delightful in the experience they wanted. So, they built one that they'd want to use. Turns out, others did, too. During the last two years, more than 1.5M users have downloaded Stardust. In early 2023, someone suggested they add a paywall in the app. That paywall consistently converted installs into paying subscribers at a serviceable rate. After more than a year, though, the paywall and pricing hadn't evolved from their first iteration and it wasn't matching the growth potential the team believed it was capable of. So, how did an app with consistent downloads grow its proceeds per user by more than 400% in only a couple of months? Let's dig in! The three growth levers Stardust used to kick-start growth When an app starts its experimentation journey, specific growth levers tend to have the most opportunity and several best practices allow those opportunities to accelerate. This is especially true if the app already has consistent traffic and baseline conversion data. 1. Start with pricing and packaging In pricing and packaging optimization, a user's perception of value has as much to do with price presentation design as the actual prices or introductory offers. It includes what product(s) you display initially, how you show comparisons between products, and what is included in those plans. In Stardust's case, they hadn't done price testing and also wanted to learn whether a free trial would increase overall paying users. Additionally, their two plans had always been displayed plainly, showing price and duration without any relative savings or equivalent prices. We identified two specific tests by asking the following questions: Will adding a free trial increase conversion rate and proceeds per user, and if so, how does changing the price impact conversions? Does optimizing the price presentation design by adding a discount percentage and equivalent pricing increase the conversion rate? Free trial and higher price test In the first experiment, the control and five price variants were tested, including price sets with and without free trials. The result was a conversion rate increase for every variant offering a free trial, including a stunning 131% increase in paywall conversion rate for the variant adding a free trial to the control's yearly price of $24.99. Higher price variants without a trial had a lower conversion rate and similar proceeds per user. The first test was paused to allow all trials to conclude so trial conversion rate data could mature; an essential part of running any price test with trials. After all trials concluded, it was clear that adding a trial increased average proceeds per user by 78% and 45% more paying subscribers . Additionally, the new variant increased the share of yearly subscriptions by more than 50% over the control. The winning variant: $24.99 per year with a free 7-day trial. Price packaging design test While the first test was paused, the second was launched, which kept the control pricing for all variants ($24.99 per year and $2.99 per week) but changed the packaging design. These three variants were tested: Add a discount percentage on the yearly plan and show weekly equivalent pricing Lead with the yearly plan and make both options visible by tapping a "More Pricing" button, revealing a product drawer Only show the yearly plan The winning variant: add a discount percentage on the yearly plan and show weekly equivalent pricing. As it turns out, showing a discount percentage on the yearly plan and weekly equivalent pricing increased the conversion rate by 50%. But more importantly, proceeds per user increased by 62.5% due to a 30% increase in the share of new yearly subscriptions. The other variants in this experiment were both conversion rate and proceeds per user losers. 2. Layer experiments and combine winners If you noticed that the second test ran while the first test's trials were still concluding and thought that was a smart idea, good for you! Timing tests like this is called experimentation layering . It's a key practice to accelerate the number of experiments you're able to run and thus influences how quickly you're able to grow. Doing this allows you to only run tests based on how long each variant takes to gather enough users into the cohort, and then run another experiment while the first test's trial conversion or retention data is gathered. At this point, Stardust had two winning variants: a set of prices with a free trial and a new price presentation design. The winning variant from test two became Stardust's new control paywall and the first variant in the new experiment would combine test 1 and 2's winners. Because there was enough traffic to run additional variants quickly, several more were added, including… The combined winners variant with a monthly plan instead of weekly Retesting a higher price variant with a trial but in the new price presentation design A combined winners variant with a video background design instead of a text-heavy design If you bet the combined winners variant would combine the growth from the first two tests, you're right. In Stardust's third test, their combined winners netted another whopping 55.7% increase over the new control and a 9% increase in proceeds per user. However, this was not the winning variant from this test. The winning variant: the combined winners variant with a video background design. With a 67% paywall conversion increase and a 12.5% proceeds per user increase, the combined winners variant with a video background showed that combining a design change was another lever to unlock for Stardust. Enter the next phase of testing. 3. Test paywall designs when you've optimized pricing and packaging Test three showed the potential of that combining design changes with optimized pricing and packaging. For test four, Stardust was eager to test a trial timeline design. The winning variant: trial timeline design. While the video background design signaled the quality of the app, showing the trial timeline design further convinced more users to start a trial (13.6% conversion rate increase) without impacting the trial-to-paid conversion rate. Total results So after several tests and compounding results, where did Stardust net out? If you recall, the app's original conversion rate was working but didn't match expectations. By the completion of the fourth test, that conversion rate had grown by 465% . Install-to-paying subscriber rate increased by 252% . Additionally, average proceeds per user increased by 408% . Finally, the increase in yearly subscriptions over the original paywall design was significant, and will be a nice revenue bonus one year from now when they renew. Unlocking Stardust's growth potential Stardust is a great product with a high-quality team behind it. With growth numbers like theirs, the question isn't why weren't they doing this before, but what was blocking it? Stardust had plenty of ideas, but they're a lean team, which doesn't often leave a lot of room for design and engineering to build, launch, and iterate on experiments. The big unlock that allowed Stardust to test their backlog of ideas was using Superwall to remotely build paywalls without code and ship A/B tests without engineering resources. They were free to run experiments at the pace of their users, not their sprint capacity. What's next for Stardust? The thing about experiment wins is they make you hungry for more. Stardust has several new experiments poised to answer new questions. They're also exploring using Superwall to experiment with other experiences as well, such as on the screens users see right before a paywall and the pregnancy tracking experience.

title: Understanding Sensitivity and Resistance to Pan-RAS(ON) Inhibition Across KRAS-Mutant Tumors
summary: To explore the complete results, figures, and molecular analyses, including responder and non-responder comparisons and acquired resistance models, download the full poster here.
body_text: Understanding Sensitivity and Resistance to Pan-RAS(ON) Inhibition Across KRAS-Mutant Tumors KRAStargeted therapies are entering a new phase of clinical relevance. Daraxonrasib, a next-generation pan-RAS(ON) inhibitor designed to target a broad spectrum of KRAS G12X mutations, has shown impressive clinical activity. In a recent Phase III RASolute 302 trial for second-line metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), daraxonrasib (RMC-6236) nearly doubled the median overall survival for patients to approximately 13.2 months, compared with 6.7 months for standard chemotherapy.1 These results highlight the rapid progress in this space. At the same time, clinical development is expanding KRAS-targeted therapies into earlier lines of therapy. Daraxonrasib is currently being evaluated in first-line settings, both as monotherapy and in combination approaches. While both clinical and preclinical data demonstrate activity across multiple tumor types, variability in response and the emergence of resistance remain key challenges that limit durable benefit. Additionally, the molecular determinants that define sensitivity, primary resistance, and acquired resistance remain incompletely understood. Addressing these gaps in our understanding of the molecular drivers of sensitivity and resistance is critical not only for patient selection but also for informing rational combination and sequencing strategies in an evolving treatment landscape. A Translational Platform to Study KRAS Biology in Context To better understand these response patterns, this study leveraged Champions Oncology’s low-passage, clinically annotated Patient-Derived Xenograft (PDX) Tumor Bank. With more than 1,500 models and extensive molecular and treatment history annotation, this platform captures both tumor heterogeneity and clinically relevant treatment context. Importantly, approximately half of the models represent pretreated disease, reflecting real-world patient populations. The translational relevance of this platform is supported by prior clinical correlation analyses performed using Champions’ low-passage PDX models. In a study by Izumchenko et al., treatment responses observed in these models were directly compared with clinical outcomes in matched patients across 92 individuals and 129 therapies.2 Strong concordance between the PDX and patient response was observed, with a positive predictive value of approximately 85% and a negative predictive value of approximately 91%. These findings establish Champions’ low-passage PDX models both as a tool for biological exploration and a clinically validated system for informing translational and drug development decisions. In this study, more than 50 KRAS-mutant PDX models were screened across non-small cell lung cancer, colorectal cancer, and pancreatic cancer (PDAC). The cohort included diverse KRAS alleles, co-occurring genomic alterations, and varying treatment histories, which allowed treatment response to be evaluated within a realistic molecular and clinical framework. Heterogeneous Responses Reflect Tumor-Specific Context Daraxonrasib treatment resulted in a broad spectrum of responses, ranging from strong disease regressions to progressive disease. Response variability was not solely explained by KRAS mutation status alone but was influenced by the broader genomic context of each tumor. For example, alterations such as MYC amplification were observed in both responding and non-responding models, suggesting that primary resistance is context-dependent and likely driven by multiple interacting genomic factors, rather than single genomic features. These findings highlight the importance of distinguishing between intrinsic resistance mechanisms and those that emerge under therapeutic pressure. Probing Primary Resistance in KRAS G12D Pancreatic Models Given the clinical relevance of KRAS G12D in pancreatic cancer, a focused analysis was performed in this subset. Differential gene expression analysis comparing responders and non-responders identified candidate markers associated with response, including MSLN and CYP24A1. While these findings are exploratory and based on a limited sample set, they provide an initial framework for stratifying tumors and generating hypotheses around mechanisms of intrinsic resistance. Ongoing work is expanding these analyses through deeper multi-omic integration, including whole exome sequencing (WES), RNA sequencing, proteomics, phosphoproteomics, and surface proteomics. These datasets will be interpreted in the context of Champions’ clinically annotated models, which include detailed treatment histories, to better understand the biological drivers of response and resistance and to support more robust biomarker development. Modeling Acquired Resistance Under Continuous Drug Pressure Selected PDX models were treated continuously beyond their initial response to investigate how resistance evolves over time. A particularly illustrative example is model CTG-2473, a KRAS G12D pancreatic cancer model derived from a tumor collected after first-line gemcitabine treatment. This model reflects a clinically relevant treatment sequence where patients, following standard chemotherapy, would be transitioned to KRAS-targeted therapies such as daraxonrasib. Therefore, treatment of CTG-2473 with daraxonrasib can model response and resistance in a post-chemotherapy setting that mirrors emerging clinical practice. Under continuous treatment pressure, this model demonstrated initial tumor regression followed by relapse, which is consistent with the development of acquired resistance observed in patients. This creates a powerful framework for translational studies. Experiments can be designed in the parental setting to evaluate therapeutic switching upon relapseto assess next-line agents or rational combination strategies. In parallel, Champions Oncology is actively developing a fully resistant subline through serial passaging under sustained drug pressure. This will enable deeper molecular characterization of acquired resistance mechanisms and provide a robust system for testing strategies for overcoming resistance. Together, these models establish a framework not only to observe resistance but also to actively model clinically relevant treatment sequencing scenarios. Why Clinically Annotated PDX Models Matter A defining strength of this work is the integration of molecular profiling, treatment response, and detailed clinical annotation within a single experimental system. Unlike conventional preclinical models, Champions’ PDX platform enables analysis of tumor behavior in the context of prior therapies, disease progression, and patient-specific treatment history. This is particularly important for targeted therapies such as KRAS inhibitors, where response and resistance are shaped by both molecular context and prior treatment. When combined with multi-omic datasets, including WES, RNA sequencing, proteomics, phosphoproteomics, and surface proteomics, these clinically annotated models provide a systems-level understanding of tumor biology. This supports the identification of candidate biomarkers and the development of mechanistically informed combination and sequencing strategies. Importantly, this integrated approach allows researchers to move beyond static response measurements tto capture how tumors dynamically adapt under therapeutic pressure and how these adaptations can be therapeutically targeted. From Mechanism to Strategy Taken together, these data demonstrate that response to pan-RAS(ON) inhibition is shaped by tumor-specific molecular context and dynamic adaptation under treatment. Understanding both primary and acquired resistance will be essential for translating KRAS-targeted therapies into durable clinical benefit. The full dataset, including detailed response profiles, genomic annotations, and resistance modeling, is presented in the accompanying poster. Download the Full Poster To explore the complete results, figures, and molecular analyses, including responder and non-responder comparisons and acquired resistance models, download the full poster here. Revolution Medicines. 2026. summary: SUZHOU, China, July 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- YXT.com Group Holding Limited (the “Company” or “YXT.com”) (NASDAQ: YXT), a provider of AI-enabled enterprise productivity solutions, today announced that it will change the ratio of its American Depositary Shares (“ADSs”) to its ordinary shares from
body_text: YXT.com Announces ADS Ratio Change to Be Effective on July 14, 2026 July 10th, 2026 PDF Version SUZHOU, China, July 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- YXT.com Group Holding Limited (the “Company” or “YXT.com”) (NASDAQ: YXT), a provider of AI-enabled enterprise productivity solutions, today announced that it will change the ratio of its American Depositary Shares (“ADSs”) to its ordinary shares from the current ratio of one (1) ADS representing three (3) ordinary shares to a new ratio of one (1) ADS representing thirty (30) ordinary shares (the “ADS Ratio Change”). The ADS Ratio Change is expected to become effective on July 14, 2026, U.S. Eastern Time (the “Effective Date”). For YXT.com’s ADS holders, the ADS Ratio Change will have the same effect as a one-for-ten reverse ADS split. There will be no change to the Company’s ordinary shares, and no ordinary shares will be issued or cancelled in connection with the ADS Ratio Change. On the Effective Date, holders of ADSs in the Direct Registration System and in The Depository Trust Company will have their ADSs automatically exchanged and need not take any action. The exchange of every ten (10) then-held existing ADSs for one (1) new ADS will occur automatically on the Effective Date, with the then-held ADSs being cancelled and new ADSs being issued by The Bank of New York Mellon, the depositary bank for the Company’s ADS program. The Company’s ADSs will continue to trade under the ticker symbol “YXT.” The new CUSIP number for the Company’s ADSs following the ADS Ratio Change will be 988740205. No fractional new ADSs will be issued in connection with the ADS Ratio Change. Instead, fractional entitlements to new ADSs will be aggregated and sold by the depositary bank, and the net cash proceeds from the sale of the fractional ADS entitlements, after deduction of applicable taxes, fees and expenses, will be distributed to the applicable ADS holders by the depositary bank in accordance with its then-current procedures and practices. As a result of the ADS Ratio Change, the ADS trading price is expected to increase proportionally, although the Company can give no assurance that the ADS trading price after the ADS Ratio Change will be equal to or greater than ten times the ADS trading price before the change. About YXT.com YXT.com (NASDAQ: YXT) is a technology company focusing on enterprise productivity solutions. With a mission to “Empower people and organization development through technology,” the Company strives to become the supreme provider in building and boosting enterprise productivity by combining over a decade of experience in tech-enabled talent learning and development and with AI-augmented task copilots and unleashing the power of knowledge and synergy. Since its inception, YXT.com has supported and received recognition from numerous Global and China Fortune 500 companies. title: Best tools to create deal rooms in 2026 (digital sales room software)
summary: The best tools to create deal rooms and digital sales rooms in 2026, compared: AI agents that generate the room's content for you, and platforms that host what you build. Twelve tools with verified G2 ratings, grouped by how much of the work they do for you.
body_text: Last updated: July 2026 The best tools to create deal rooms (also called digital sales room software) in 2026 are Mutiny, Dock, Aligned, GetAccept, Allego, Seismic, Highspot, Showpad, Mindtickle, DocSend, PandaDoc, and Qwilr. They divide into two groups: tools that generate the room’s content for you, and tools that host and track content you build yourself. Here is the quick version of who each one is for: Mutiny: best overall for teams that want the room’s content generated for them and the follow-up automated. Dock: best full-lifecycle buyer workspace, from sales room to onboarding. Aligned: best for complex deals with large buying committees. GetAccept: best for a deal room with proposals and e-signature built in. Allego: best for video-first sales enablement with a deal room attached. Seismic: best for enterprise sales enablement at scale. Highspot: best for enablement content management with a DSR. Showpad: best for content centralization and engagement analytics. Mindtickle: best for sales readiness and enablement with a DSR. DocSend: best for page-level document engagement tracking. PandaDoc: best for proposals and e-signature in the room. Qwilr: best for design-forward, web-based proposals. The biggest difference between these tools is how much of the room’s content each one writes for you. Mutiny drafts a personalized business case, pricing, and next steps per account, then automates the follow-up around it. The other tools focus on hosting and tracking content the rep assembles by hand. This guide covers what a deal room is, why they matter, the four types of tools, what to look for, all twelve tools with verified G2 ratings, and the data on how deal rooms affect win rates. What is a deal room? A deal room, also called a digital sales room, is a shared and personalized web space where a seller and a buying group access everything tied to a deal through one link: the business case, pricing, demos, references, a mutual action plan, and next steps. It replaces scattered email attachments and gives sellers visibility into who engaged with what. For the full breakdown, see what a deal room should include . A sales deal room and an M&A data room are different things that share a name. This guide covers the sales deal room, a buyer-facing space for selling and closing a deal. It does not cover the virtual data room (VDR) used to store diligence documents in mergers, acquisitions, and fundraising. If you are running an M&A process, you want a data room. Why do deal rooms matter in 2026? Deal rooms matter because buyers now spend most of the cycle away from reps. Gartner reports that B2B buyers spend only 17% of their total purchase journey meeting with potential suppliers , and that 67% of buyers say they prefer a rep-free experience . A deal room is how sellers stay useful during the roughly 80% of the journey they are not in the room. Buying groups have also grown. Gartner puts the typical B2B buying group at six to ten decision-makers , each doing independent research and internal deliberation. A deal room gives the champion one link to forward internally, so more of that off-line evaluation happens on content the seller controls. What are the types of digital sales room tools? Digital sales room tools fall into four categories, ordered from most to least hands-off on the actual content. Most tools host content the rep builds elsewhere. Only the AI generator category produces the room’s content for you. AI deal room generators: create the room’s content (a personalized business case, pricing, and next steps) from your CRM and call context. Mutiny leads here. Buyer portals and end-to-end DSR platforms: host and organize content in a shared buyer workspace with engagement tracking. Dock, Aligned, and GetAccept sit here. Sales enablement platforms with a DSR: large content and training systems that added a deal room feature. Allego, Seismic, Highspot, Showpad, and Mindtickle sit here. Document and proposal tools: link-based sharing, proposals, and e-signature with room-style bundling. DocSend, PandaDoc, and Qwilr sit here. What should a deal room include? A strong deal room includes six components: a personalized business case, tailored pricing, a mutual action plan, relevant proof, product demos or recordings, and clear next steps. The best rooms are built for the specific account and updated as the deal moves, so the buying group always sees current, relevant content. Personalized business case: the problem, cost of inaction, and ROI framed for this buyer. See the best tools to create a business case . Tailored pricing: the specific proposal, not a generic rate card. Mutual action plan: shared steps and dates to signature. Proof: case studies, references, and security or compliance documents relevant to the account. Demos and recordings: product walkthroughs and key call moments the champion can forward internally. Next steps: an unambiguous call to action so momentum holds. What should you look for in a deal room tool? Look for five things: how much of the content the tool creates for you, how well it personalizes to the account, what engagement analytics it surfaces, how easily any rep can run it without design or marketing help, and whether the surrounding workflow can be automated. The largest differences show up in the first factor, because most tools host content the rep still has to build somewhere else. Content generation: does it draft the business case, pricing, and narrative, or only display files you made elsewhere? Personalization: can it tailor the room to the specific account automatically? Engagement analytics: does it show who viewed what, so reps can time follow-ups? Self-serve usability: can an AE spin one up on day one without a GTM engineer? Workflow automation: can the surrounding work (follow-ups, updates, recaps) run automatically instead of by hand? The 12 best tools to create deal rooms in 2026 1. Mutiny Mutiny is the AI-native tool for creating personalized deal content and automating the GTM workflow around it. For deal rooms, Mutiny generates the room’s content itself: a personalized business case, tailored pricing, competitive comparisons, and next steps built for the specific account, in minutes. It works as a two-sided model. The agent creates the customer-facing assets inside the room, and reps and marketers build their own agents and routines to automate the busywork around the deal, from follow-ups to keeping the room current as things change. Any AE, BDR, marketer, or CSM can run it on day one with no GTM engineer required, and it ships with a deal room blueprint so teams start from a working example rather than a blank page. Best for: teams that want the deal room content generated and the follow-up automated end to end. Key features: AI-generated business case, pricing, and next steps per account; two-sided agent plus automation model; day-one self-serve for any rep; prebuilt deal room blueprint; built-in engagement analytics. Pricing: Free, Business, and Enterprise custom plans (starting at $30k). See pricing . “My champion said nobody gave her anything like what I gave her. This makes it so much easier for me to show them everything that we’ve walked through and done.” Jeff Goldberg, Account Executive, Kaizen 2. Dock Dock is a customer-facing workspace used for sales rooms, onboarding plans, and client portals across the full customer lifecycle. It organizes the content a rep assembles into a clean, shared buyer workspace, tracks engagement across the buying group, and carries the same link from sales into onboarding and renewals. Dock holds a 4.9 out of 5 on G2 . Best for: teams that want one polished workspace from deal to onboarding. Key features: flexible deal rooms, prebuilt widgets, mutual action plans, order forms and e-signature, engagement analytics, and Salesforce and HubSpot sync. What reviewers say: G2 reviewers praise Dock as a clean hub for sharing content with buyers; the most common critiques mention occasional bugs and time spent on initial template setup. 3. Aligned Aligned is a buyer collaboration platform built around digital sales rooms and mutual action plans. It gives sellers and buying committees a structured shared space to coordinate a deal, with the rep supplying the content and Aligned handling organization and visibility. Aligned holds a 4.7 out of 5 on G2 and ranks at the top of G2’s digital sales room grid. Best for: complex deals with large buying committees that need a structured action plan. Key features: digital sales rooms, mutual action plans, stakeholder tracking, content engagement analytics, and CRM signals surfaced in pipeline reviews. What reviewers say: G2 reviewers highlight the intuitive interface, centralized communication, and team collaboration as standouts. 4. GetAccept GetAccept is a combined deal room, proposal, and e-signature platform. It splits the workflow into a deal room for the early stages and a contract room for proposal to signature, which makes it one of the more end-to-end options for teams that live in quotes and contracts. GetAccept holds a 4.6 out of 5 on G2 . Best for: teams that want the deal room, proposals, and signatures in one place. Key features: deal rooms, proposals and contracts with templates, e-signature, sales content management, personalized video, and engagement tracking. What reviewers say: G2 reviewers cite ease of use, proposal tracking, personalized video, and faster proposal turnaround. 5. Allego Allego is a video-first sales enablement and training platform that added digital sales room functionality on top of its coaching and content tools. It fits teams whose primary need is enablement and rep readiness, with a deal room as a secondary layer. Allego holds a 4.6 out of 5 on G2 . Best for: teams that want video-centric enablement and coaching with a deal room attached. Key features: video coaching, content management, document sharing, deal room content tracking, and strong data security. What reviewers say: reviewers describe Allego as a modern, real-world enablement platform focused on on-demand learning; some note DSR setup can feel clunky. 6. Seismic Seismic is the enterprise standard in sales enablement, a broad content and readiness platform that added digital sales room tools more recently. It suits large sales organizations that want a comprehensive enablement system and can absorb the setup investment. Seismic holds a 4.6 out of 5 on G2 . Best for: enterprise sales teams that want deep enablement with a DSR alongside it. Key features: content management, LiveDocs, buyer engagement analytics, DSR templates, and buyer privacy settings. What reviewers say: reviewers call Seismic the most comprehensive enablement platform in the market; the common friction points are a steep learning curve and total cost of ownership. 7. Highspot Highspot is a sales enablement and content management platform with a digital sales room feature for sharing curated content externally. It fits teams that want strong content governance and AI-assisted search, with the DSR as one surface among many. Highspot holds a 4.7 out of 5 on G2 . Best for: teams that prioritize enablement content management with an external DSR. Key features: content management and governance, AI search, buyer-facing content pages, and engagement analytics. What reviewers say: ease of use is the most-cited positive on G2; the common complaint is search and findability once the content library grows large. 8. Showpad Showpad is a revenue enablement platform focused on content centralization, engagement analytics, and coaching, with deal room style sharing for buyers. It suits teams that want to centralize collateral and measure how buyers interact with it. Showpad holds a 4.6 out of 5 on G2 . Best for: teams that want content centralization and engagement analytics. Key features: content management, buyer engagement analytics, coaching, and external content sharing. What reviewers say: reviewers value content centralization and analytics; Gartner named Showpad a Leader in its 2025 Magic Quadrant for Revenue Enablement Platforms. 9. Mindtickle Mindtickle is a sales readiness and revenue enablement platform that pairs training and coaching with a digital sales room. It fits teams that want to connect rep readiness to buyer-facing rooms, and it publishes some of the most-cited data on DSR win rates. Mindtickle holds a 4.7 out of 5 on G2 . Best for: teams that want sales readiness and enablement with a DSR. Key features: training and readiness, coaching, content management, digital sales rooms, and buyer engagement analytics. What reviewers say: reviewers highlight comprehensive training modules and content quality; the DSR is a newer layer on a mature enablement platform. 10. DocSend DocSend, now part of Dropbox, focuses on secure document sharing with page-by-page engagement analytics. Sellers share a link and see exactly which sections a prospect viewed, which makes it useful for tracking interest in a specific document or deck. DocSend holds a 4.6 out of 5 on G2 . Best for: tracking engagement on individual documents and decks. Key features: secure link sharing, page-level view analytics, access controls, and document rooms. What reviewers say: reviewers praise the engagement tracking and ease of setup; it is a document tool first, not a full buyer workspace. 11. PandaDoc PandaDoc is a document workflow platform for proposals, quotes, and e-signature, with room-style sharing for bundling deal documents. It is strong on the contract and signature side of a deal. PandaDoc holds a 4.7 out of 5 on G2 . Best for: teams that need proposals and e-signature tightly integrated. Key features: proposal and quote builder, templates, e-signature, real-time tracking, and CRM integrations. What reviewers say: reviewers cite ease of use, templates, e-signature, and real-time tracking; PandaDoc was voted the top contract management tool for small business in G2’s Spring 2026 report. 12. Qwilr Qwilr turns proposals and sales content into interactive web pages with built-in analytics. It is a design-forward way to present a proposal as a branded page rather than a static PDF. Qwilr holds a 4.6 out of 5 on G2 . Best for: visually polished, web-based proposals. Key features: interactive web proposals, accept and pay, e-signature, and page-level analytics. What reviewers say: reviewers describe Qwilr as a visually powerful proposal tool that speeds up turnaround and makes proposals stand out. How do the top deal room tools compare? Tool Best for Approach to deal room content Mutiny Generating content and automating the workflow AI drafts a personalized business case, pricing, and next steps per account; reps automate the surrounding follow-ups Dock Full-lifecycle buyer workspace Hosts and organizes content the rep assembles, from sales room to onboarding Aligned Large buying committees Structured buyer-seller workspace; rep supplies content GetAccept Deal room plus proposals and e-signature Hosts content and handles quotes, contracts, and signatures Allego Video-first enablement Enablement and coaching platform with a DSR layer Seismic Enterprise enablement Comprehensive content system with a DSR added Highspot Enablement content management Content governance and search with an external DSR Showpad Content and engagement analytics Content centralization with buyer engagement tracking Mindtickle Sales readiness plus DSR Readiness and coaching platform with a DSR DocSend Document engagement tracking Link-based sharing with page-level analytics PandaDoc Proposals and e-signature Document workflows with room-style sharing Qwilr Design-forward proposals Interactive web proposal pages with analytics Do deal rooms actually improve win rates? Yes. According to Mindtickle’s 2025 State of Revenue Enablement Report , deals with an associated digital sales room had a 26% higher win rate, closed 30% bigger, and moved through 10% shorter sales cycles. How do you create a deal room? At a high level: start from a template, personalize the business case and pricing to the account, add proof and a mutual action plan, and share one link.
